package_info.why_malicious: These package versions were hijacked via compromised npm tokens and had malicious, heavily obfuscated code injected into their distribution files. The injected code downloads and executes a Monero (XMR) cryptocurrency miner (XMRig) on the victim's system, connects to a hardcoded mining pool using a specific wallet address, and attempts to communicate with an external command-and-control server, resulting in unauthorized resource usage, potential data exfiltration, and further compromise.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (when the package is loaded or executed as part of a build or CLI operation)
execution_context.file_location: dist/utils/config.js in @rspack/cli and @rspack/core; support.js in vant
required_permissions: filesystem (to write and execute binaries in /tmp)
network (to download binaries and contact external servers)
process (to spawn child processes for curl, chmod, and miner execution)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code uses Node.js child_process to download and execute the XMRig Monero miner binary from a remote server, connects to a hardcoded mining pool with a specific wallet address, and initiates an outbound HTTPS request to a command-and-control server, resulting in unauthorized cryptocurrency mining and potential exfiltration or further malicious activity.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is heavily obfuscated and embedded in utility files that should not contain such logic. It downloads and executes an external binary (XMRig miner) from a remote server, spawns multiple system processes (curl, chmod, miner), and establishes outbound network connections to both a mining pool and a suspicious hardcoded IP address, all without user knowledge or consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate package utility or configuration files should not download or execute external binaries, initiate cryptocurrency mining, or contact unknown external servers during import or execution. Such actions are outside the scope of normal package behavior and represent a clear abuse of user trust.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some packages may contact external servers for telemetry or updates, but this should be transparent, documented, and never involve downloading and executing untrusted binaries or mining cryptocurrency. Automated update mechanisms should use secure channels and not run arbitrary code.
key_indicators: Heavily obfuscated code present in utility or support files
Use of child_process.exec to run system commands (curl, chmod, miner execution)
Download and execution of XMRig miner binary from a remote server
Hardcoded Monero wallet address in miner command
Outbound HTTPS connection to hardcoded suspicious IP (80.78.28.72)
Creation of new executable file in /tmp directory
No legitimate reason for such behavior in a JavaScript bundler or UI library

attack_chain.action: User installs or updates the compromised package, which includes the obfuscated malicious code in its distribution files.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is loaded and executed on the victim's system during package import or execution.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code downloads the XMRig Monero miner binary from a remote server, writes it to /tmp, sets executable permissions, and executes it with a hardcoded wallet address and mining pool.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim's system resources are hijacked for unauthorized cryptocurrency mining, potentially degrading performance and increasing operational costs.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code establishes an outbound HTTPS connection to an external command-and-control server at 80.78.28.72.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential exfiltration of data, receipt of further instructions, or tracking of infected hosts by the attacker.

behavioral_signatures: Presence of heavily obfuscated JavaScript code in utility or configuration files (e.g., config.js, support.js)
Use of child_process.exec or similar APIs to invoke system commands (curl, chmod, execution of binaries) during package import or execution
Download and execution of external binaries (such as XMRig) from remote servers
Outbound network connections to hardcoded IP addresses or domains unrelated to package functionality
Creation of new executable files in temporary directories (e.g., /tmp/xmrig) by Node.js processes
file_indicators: dist/utils/config.js (obfuscated, new or modified in malicious versions of @rspack/cli and @rspack/core)
support.js in vant (obfuscated, new or modified in malicious versions)
/tmp/xmrig or similar miner binary dropped to disk after package execution
network_indicators: Outbound connections to Monero mining pool pool.minexmr.com:4444
Unexpected outbound traffic to unknown or suspicious IPs/domains immediately after package installation or import
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for obfuscated or unexpected code in package distribution files, especially in dist/utils/config.js and support.js. Detect post-install or import-time execution of external binaries, particularly known miners like XMRig, by monitoring process creation events involving curl, chmod, or non-standard binaries executed by Node.js. Flag any package that initiates outbound connections to suspicious IPs (e.g., 80.78.28.72) or mining pools (e.g., pool.minexmr.com:4444). Use file integrity monitoring to detect new or modified files such as /tmp/xmrig. Correlate these behaviors to identify malicious activity and prevent further compromise.
